knowledge_graph.title: Chronic liver disease
knowledge_graph.description: Chronic liver disease in the clinical context is a disease process of the liver that involves a process of progressive destruction and regeneration of the liver parenchyma leading to fibrosis and cirrhosis. "Chronic liver disease" refers to disease of the liver which lasts over a period of six months.

text_blocks.snippet: Chronic hepatocellular disease refers to a long-term, progressive condition where the liver's hepatocytes (liver cells) are damaged, leading to impaired liver function. It's a spectrum of liver diseases that persist for at least six months. This damage can result in scarring (cirrhosis) and potentially hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer).
snippet_highlighted_words: a long-term, progressive condition where the liver's hepatocytes (liver cells) are damaged, leading to impaired liver function

list.snippet: Progressive Damage: The liver cells (hepatocytes) are continuously damaged over time.
Long-Term Condition: The disease lasts for six months or longer.
